intent: Keep bootstrap and runtime credential dotenv files private from their first byte under a permissive Linux umask, and narrow existing files before reading, appending or backing them up. Cover Hermes .env, its backups and PatterStage .env.local, which setup copies the Hermes API key into. Preserve Windows and Git Bash setup behaviour.

reasons.evidence: Credential-file permissions are a security boundary; independent executable acceptance precedes implementation, and the full gate plus mutation sweep is required.

programme: Prerequisite T-0163 after the T-0162 blind-gate repair, before T-0158 browser sessions. No release-gated removal or public CLI change is claimed.
invariants: On Linux, a fresh credential file and every staging or backup file containing its bytes is owner-only from creation even under umask 000.
An existing group/world-readable credential file is narrowed before setup or runtime reads or appends, and failure to secure it fails closed without printing credentials.
Existing dotenv keys, comments and ordering survive permitted rewrites; no configured key or documented setup path is removed.
Windows and Git Bash setup remain functional; POSIX mode assertions run on Linux rather than pretending Windows mode bits enforce secrecy.
Independent executable acceptance is frozen before source changes; amendments require a different author.
notes: At T-0162 close, scripts/bootstrap/setup.sh touches Hermes .env under the caller's umask; setup.mjs appends with default mode; env-local.mjs writes PatterStage .env.local with default mode; hermes-config-write.ts stages .env with default mode; shared backupFile writes plaintext with default mode. This task includes those paths because a secure bootstrap alone would be undone by the next runtime credential write. T-0162 push and PR CI remain in progress; any hosted failure is repaired before T-0163 lands. The declaration-only EOS router returned R0 with no discrepancies; the operator's security R2 floor remains binding, and the actual diff is reruled upward at the gate.
rollback: Revert the permission change and its oracle as a unit only if a replacement security fix is ready; otherwise rollback reopens world-readable credential files. Test both setup paths and runtime writes under a permissive Linux umask and repeat the full gate.
